title: The porter learns each replacement from how the game ported its own code
text: GameDiff knew three shapes of change in the game's own code (a call switched, one added argument with its default, a chain). For every game method that used a changed or removed member and still exists in the next release, both bodies are rebuilt as value trees from their bytecode and lined up through the links; what the new code computes at the use, written over the old member's operands, is the replacement, in the same form as a rule's inClass, so JarPort applies it with no second path. The game's own uses vote, and a constant two operands share is settled across uses.
finish: port.game-learned up from 1,413 over all 43 updates, port.jar-links up, and every linked standalone mod loads on a real 1.21.2 server
wrongIf: a mod that links only because of a learned replacement fails on the server
result: 2026-11-19: 1,413 -> 2,462 of 49,503 gone members get a replacement over all 43 updates (port.game-learned). On top of #120, 43 -> 45 of 150 NeoForge 1.21.1 mods link on 1.21.2 (Controlling and TerraBlender), broken references 4,556 -> 4,425. On a real 1.21.2 server 24 of the 26 that link load and 1 is client-only; TerraBlender fails on a biome data file 1.21.2 cannot parse (the same error as before it linked), which no link check sees. Left: redesigns, value-to-value changes an expression cannot say, and data files.
